config.statsInfoOverviewMsg: A snapshot of your entire bookmark library: how many pages, categories, and bookmarks exist, and how often they are opened on average.
config.statsInfoInboxMsg: How your inbox is doing. The current inbox shows what's queued right now, including how stale unread items are. Triage throughput tracks lifetime counters — how many links you saved, converted to bookmarks, or discarded — and the conversion rate shows whether your inbox is a useful queue or a black hole. Lifetime counters start from when tracking began, so older activity isn't included.
config.statsInfoHealthMsg: A summary of the Health view. Healthy bookmarks passed every check; broken ones failed a reachability check; unchecked ones haven't been tested yet. The breakdown counts the other issues Health flags — duplicate URLs, shortcut conflicts, stale checks, missing previews, and unused bookmarks. Open the Health view from the dashboard to inspect and fix individual bookmarks.
config.statsInfoInsightsMsg: Automated highlights from your library: busiest page, top bookmark, never-opened share, status coverage, and recent activity in the last 48 hours. Links jump to the related section below.
config.statsInfoScoreMsg: A 0–100 score based on library health. Penalties: bookmarks never opened (up to −25), not visited in 90+ days (up to −20), duplicate URLs (up to −15), conflicting shortcuts (up to −10).
config.statsInfoActivityMsg: The sparkline counts bookmarks whose last-open timestamp falls in each bucket — a recency view, not individual opens. The total sums lifetime openCount for bookmarks active in the period (lastOpened within the window). All time uses the last 12 months.
config.statsInfoTopMsg: When a period is selected, only bookmarks opened within that window are listed. Opens shows lifetime openCount, not opens within the period. The bar is relative to the highest value in the list.
config.statsInfoPagesMsg: Bookmark counts per page. With a period filter, only bookmarks opened in that window are included; Opens sums their lifetime openCount. The bar reflects totals relative to the busiest page.
config.statsInfoCategoriesMsg: Bookmark counts per category and page. With a period filter, only bookmarks opened in that window are included; Opens sums their lifetime openCount.
config.statsInfoTagsMsg: Tag coverage across your library. With a period filter, open totals include only bookmarks opened in that window and show lifetime openCount — not opens within the period.
config.statsInfoShortcutsMsg: Coverage bar showing how many bookmarks have a shortcut assigned. The table lists the top 20 shortcuts ranked by open count.
config.statsInfoFindersMsg: Usage stats for custom search finders from the Finders tab. useCount increments when you open a finder from the dashboard.
config.statsInfoRotMsg: 'Never opened' lists bookmarks with zero opens ever. 'Stale' lists bookmarks not opened within the selected period. Use the Health page to archive or remove them.
config.statsInfoConflictsMsg: Duplicate URLs are bookmarks sharing the same address. Shortcut conflicts occur when a shortcut is assigned to more than one bookmark. Use the Health page to resolve them.
config.statsInfoSearchMsg: A snapshot of your current search and monitoring settings: whether the search index is built, which modes are active, and how many bookmarks have status checks enabled.

Disabled:

config.packedColumnsInfoMessage:
When enabled, bookmark/category blocks are distributed round-robin across columns on wider screens.

• Reduces empty vertical gaps
• Can make reading order feel less top-to-bottom
• Saved instantly when toggled
config.showSyncToastsInfoMessage:
Show or hide cross-tab sync toasts.

• On: brief confirmation when another tab applies config/settings updates
• Off: no sync popup noise, but sync still happens
config.allowLocalBookmarksInfoMessage:
When enabled, bookmarks may use http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, and private LAN IPs. Status checks, link previews, auto-heal, and icon downloads from URLs can reach those hosts.

• On by default for local dev workflows
• Turn off if nextDash is exposed on a shared network (SSRF hardening)
config.globalShortcutsInfoMessage:
When enabled, shortcuts from every page can be used anywhere.

• Faster launch across pages
• Higher chance of shortcut conflicts if duplicates exist
config.showBookmarkStatusInfoMessage:
Two levels: this switch enables dashboard status globally. Each bookmark also needs its own status check under Config → Bookmarks.

• Useful for service links, but adds network checks
config.statusTwoLevelHint: Dashboard status is global. Each bookmark also needs its own status check enabled under Config → Bookmarks.
config.statusEssentialsHint: Per-bookmark checks (as in onboarding) live under Bookmarks. Health shows issues across all pages. Advanced: retries, colors, and ping.
config.statusEssentialsSummaryOnNone: On · no bookmarks with status checks yet
config.skipFastPingInfoMessage:
Changes how status checks run.

• Off: quick connectivity ping first, then HTTP check
• On: skip quick ping and run HTTP-only check
• Use if fast ping causes false negatives in your setup
config.statusOfflineRetriesInfoMessage:
How many failed ping attempts are needed before a bookmark is marked offline.

• Default: 3
• Range: 1–10
• Higher values reduce false alarms on flaky networks
config.statusOfflineRetryDelayInfoMessage:
Pause between retry pings within one status check.

• Default: 450 ms
• Range: 100–3000 ms
• Only applies while retries are still running
config.statusRecheckIntervalInfoMessage:
How often visible bookmarks are checked again in the background.

• Default: 5 minutes
• Shorter intervals use more network requests
config.healthRecheckEnabledLabel: Re-check bookmark health in the background
config.healthRecheckInfoMessage:
Periodically re-pings status-checked bookmarks on the server, so the Health view stays current without a manual "Retest all".

• Runs on the server — no browser needs to be open
• Off by default; it makes outbound requests
• Broken rows are revisited so a recovered link clears itself
config.backupsIntro: Back up and restore your entire dashboard — pages, categories, bookmarks, finders, settings, and custom themes. Use the ZIP backup to safeguard your data or move it to another device. Import browser bookmarks as a starting point, or export all bookmarks to CSV for use in spreadsheet tools.
config.backupsBrowserImportHint: Export bookmarks from Chrome, Firefox, or Edge as HTML and import here. Folders become categories; duplicate URLs are skipped. Missing icons are fetched automatically with a progress bar.
config.backupsCsvExportHint: Downloads all bookmarks from all pages as a single CSV file (name, URL, category, page, shortcut, tags, notes). Opens in Excel, Google Sheets, or any text editor.
config.backupInfo: Downloads a ZIP with bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, custom themes (colors.json), uploaded dashboard favicon/font, and bookmark icon files (data/icons/).
config.backupError: Failed to create backup. Please try again.
config.autoBackupsIntro: A backup is created automatically every week and stored on the server. The latest 3 are kept — the oldest is removed when a newer one is made.
config.autoBackupRunError: Failed to create backup. Please try again.
config.autoBackupDeleteConfirmMessage: Delete this backup? This cannot be undone.
config.autoBackupRestoreConfirmMessage: Restore this backup? This replaces all current data and cannot be undone.
config.importInfo:
Select a ZIP exported from nextDash to restore bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, themes, branding uploads, and icon files. This replaces your current data.

Bookmark URL rules use allowLocalBookmarks from the imported settings.json when that file is in the ZIP.

Important: Do not modify or rename files inside the ZIP, as this may cause import errors.
config.importSuccess: Data imported successfully! The page will reload.
config.importSuccessSkipped: Import completed. {count} bookmark(s) with disallowed URLs were skipped.
config.importError: Failed to import data. Please try again.
config.importInvalidFile: Invalid file. Please select a valid nextDash backup ZIP file.
config.importConfirmMessage: This will replace all your current bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, themes, branding uploads, and icon files with the data from the selected ZIP. This action cannot be undone. Continue?
config.browserImportNoNew: All URLs from this file already exist on the selected page — nothing to import.
config.browserImportInvalidFile: Please select a browser bookmark HTML export file.
config.browserImportEmpty: No valid bookmarks found in the file.
config.csvExportError: Failed to export bookmarks to CSV.
config.browserImportModalUnavailable: Could not open the import dialog. Refresh the page and try again.
config.settingsExportHint: Downloads your current settings as JSON. Does not include bookmarks, pages, or themes.
config.settingsImportHint: Overwrites current settings with a previously exported JSON file.
config.settingsImportInvalidFile: Please select a valid settings JSON file.
config.settingsImportConfirmMessage: This will overwrite your current settings. Continue?
config.fuzzySuggestionsStartWith: Only show suggestions that start with the query
config.fuzzySuggestionsInfoMessage:
When enabled, shows additional bookmark suggestions in shortcut search that contain the typed letters anywhere in their name.

For example:
• Typing 'ho' will show bookmarks like 'HomePage', 'PhotoShop', etc.
• Works alongside existing shortcut matches
• Can be further filtered with the sub-option below
config.includeFindersInSearchInfoMessage:
When enabled, you can access finders directly from the main search.

• Type a finder shortcut (e.g., "YT") and press space to automatically switch to finder mode.
• If a bookmark has the same shortcut as a finder, both options will appear for selection.
config.keepSearchOpenWhenEmptyInfoMessage:
When enabled, the search UI stays open even with an empty query.

• Good for keyboard-only workflows
• Can feel busier if you prefer a minimal idle state
config.showTagCloudButtonInfoMessage: Shows a / button stacked with What's new (desktop). Press / or click to open a tag word cloud (larger = more used). Click or Enter/Space toggles tags in the filter — the modal stays open so you can combine several. Bookmarks match any selected tag (OR). Active tags appear as chips under the title (each with ×) and on the / FAB (#work +1 when multiple). Arrow keys move between tags and Clear tag filter. Escape in the cloud closes the modal; Escape on the dashboard clears all filters. Clear tag filter removes every tag. • Related: :tag work in command mode lists bookmarks in the palette without changing the dashboard • Desktop / wide layout only — hidden on mobile • On by default (desktop only) • Turn off here to hide the button and modal entirely
config.showPageTabsInfoMessage:
Controls whether page navigation tabs are visible.

• On: click/tap tabs to switch pages
• Off: switch pages using keyboard shortcuts only
config.showPageNamesInTabsInfoMessage:
Controls tab labels when tabs are visible.

• On: show page names
• Off: show page numbers
config.hideEmptyCategoriesInfoMessage:
When enabled, categories with no bookmarks are hidden on the dashboard.

• Keeps the dashboard tidy
• Empty categories are still visible in config → categories
config.alwaysCollapseCategoriesInfoMessage:
When enabled, categories start collapsed when dashboard data loads.

• Cleaner first view
• Requires extra clicks to open content each session
config.categoriesRecovered: Recovered missing categories from bookmark references and saved them.
config.deviceSpecificEnabled: Device-specific settings enabled. Settings will now be stored locally.
config.deviceSpecificDisabled: Device-specific settings disabled. Current values will be saved to global settings when you click Save.
config.removePageMessage: Are you sure you want to remove the page "{pageName}"? All bookmarks in this page will be deleted. This action cannot be undone.
config.unsavedChangesLeaveConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page?
config.unsavedChangesSavePrompt: Save changes before leaving this page?
config.unsavedChangesLeaveMessage: All unsaved changes will be lost.
config.unsavedColorChangesLeaveConfirm: You have unsaved color changes. Leave this page?
config.unsavedColorChangesSavePrompt: Save color changes before leaving this page?
config.configSavedReturnDashboard: Settings saved — return to the dashboard to see changes.
config.configSavedReturnDashboardDuplicates: Settings saved. Duplicate bookmark URLs detected — return to the dashboard to review.
config.bookmarkUrlHostNotAllowed: A bookmark uses a local or private URL. Enable Allow local bookmarks in General → Advanced, or change the URL.
config.resetSectionHint: Delete all pages, categories, bookmarks, finders, and settings — then start from the default sample dashboard.
config.resetSectionCleared: Also clears custom theme colours, uploaded favicon/font, bookmark icons, and health/preview caches. Default sample bookmarks (with favicons prefetched) and built-in settings are recreated.
config.resetAllDataMessage: This permanently deletes all pages, categories, bookmarks, finders, settings, custom themes, uploaded favicon/font, bookmark icons, and caches. You start over with default sample bookmarks and built-in settings. This cannot be undone.
config.resetAllDataButton: Reset all data and start over
config.deleteAllBookmarksHint: Removes every bookmark on every page. Your pages, categories, and all settings stay exactly as they are — and no default sample bookmarks are added back. This cannot be undone.
config.deleteAllBookmarksMessage: This permanently deletes every bookmark on every page. Your pages, categories, finders, and all settings stay exactly as they are. No default sample bookmarks are added back. This cannot be undone.
config.deleteAllBookmarksTypePrompt: Type DELETE to confirm deleting all bookmarks:
config.deleteAllBookmarksTypeMismatch: Deletion cancelled: confirmation text did not match.
config.pwaInstallHint: Install nextDash for launcher-style access (pairs well with HyprMode).
config.pwaInstallReady: Install is available on this device.
config.pwaInstallAlreadyInstalled: Installed — nextDash is running as an app.
config.pwaInstallStepsIos:
1. Open the dashboard in Safari.
  2. Tap Share → Add to Home Screen.
  3. Enable HyprMode above for launcher behaviour.
config.pwaInstallStepsAndroid:
1. Open the dashboard in Chrome.
  2. Tap the menu → Install app or Add to Home screen.
  3. Enable HyprMode above for launcher behaviour.
config.pwaInstallStepsChrome:
1. Open the dashboard in Chrome.
  2. Click the install icon in the address bar or menu → Install nextDash.
  3. Enable HyprMode above for launcher behaviour.
config.pwaInstallStepsEdge:
1. Open the dashboard in Edge.
  2. Menu → Apps → Install this site as an app.
  3. Enable HyprMode above for launcher behaviour.
config.pwaInstallStepsDesktop:
1. Open the dashboard in your browser.
  2. Use the browser menu → Install app or Add to Home screen.
  3. Enable HyprMode above for launcher behaviour.

config.structureWorkspaceFootnote: Reorder, archive, templates, icons, and merge: use the Pages and Categories tabs.

config.hyprModeInfoMessage: HyprMode is designed for when nextDash is installed as a Progressive Web App (PWA). When enabled, clicking on bookmarks will open them in a new browser tab and then automatically close the PWA window, mimicking the behavior of a traditional app launcher.
config.resetOnboardingHint: Show the quick-start card again on the dashboard (language, layout, weather, then the checklist). Saves immediately.
config.resetOnboardingSuccess: Onboarding reset. Open the dashboard to see the quick-start card.

config.resetConfigBookmarksTourFailed: Could not start the Bookmarks tour. Open the Bookmarks tab first.
config.resetConfigBookmarksTourFailedTab: Could not start the Bookmarks tour. Open the Bookmarks tab first.

config.configBookmarksTourWelcomeBody: List on the left, detail editor on the right. The Context panel above stays collapsed until you need to switch page or category.
config.configBookmarksTourListControlsBody: Pick page and category, change sort, search below, and use + Bookmark for Add & edit (needs Save) or Quick add (⚡, saves immediately).
config.configBookmarksTourStructureBody: The Context panel switches the active page and category for the bookmark list. Reorder pages or categories on the dedicated Pages and Categories tabs.
config.configBookmarksTourPageFilterBody: Choose which dashboard page you edit. Filter by category or change sort order in large collections.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentStepBody: Optional: we add temporary demo bookmarks, then remove them before you finish.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentMessage: We add a couple of temporary bookmarks with random public websites, then remove them before you finish the tour.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentYesBody: Great — we use random public sites as examples. First: a bookmark in the list and editor (not saved to disk until you click Save).
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentNoBody: Skipped the live demos. Open + Bookmark anytime for Add & edit or Quick add (⚡).
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoIntroBody: Open + Bookmark → Add & edit. It adds a row and opens the editor — click Save when you are done.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoDoneBody: Edit name, URL, category, and more on the right. This demo row stays in the editor until you click Save — it is not on the dashboard yet.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoFailBody: Open + Bookmark → Add & edit to create a bookmark, then fill name and URL on the right.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddBody: Quick add (⚡) saves immediately — unlike Add & edit, no Save click needed.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddDoneBody: Quick add writes straight to disk — no Save click. The bookmark appears in the list and on the dashboard.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddFailBody: Open + Bookmark → Quick add (⚡) to add a bookmark that saves immediately.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorBody: Edit name, URL, shortcut, category, tags, pin, and status. Fetch favicon and link previews here.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenIntroBody: Quick add (⚡) opens the same bookmark modal as the dashboard + button.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenDoneBody: Quick add uses the same + modal as the dashboard. Name and URL are prefilled — Create saves immediately to this page.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenFailBody: Click Quick add (⚡) to open the + bookmark modal.
config.configBookmarksTourModalWizardIntroBody: The tour card stays at the bottom; the + modal stays in the center so you can use both.
config.configBookmarksTourModalWizardBody: On small screens the + modal is a short wizard: URL first, then name and options.
config.configBookmarksTourModalDesktopBody: On desktop you see the full form at once. The tour card stays beside the modal so fields stay readable.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveIntroBody: Creating here writes the bookmark to disk immediately — no Config Save click needed.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveDoneBody: That bookmark was saved straight to disk (unlike editor-only changes). It appears in the list and on the dashboard.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveFailBody: The demo could not be saved automatically — you can create one with Quick add (⚡) yourself.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardIntroBody: The dashboard toolbar + button opens this modal too. We visit the dashboard next.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardHandoffBody: Next we open the dashboard briefly: the + toolbar button uses this same modal. Click Next to continue there, then you return here to clean up.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardToolbarBody: Press + or click this button to add a bookmark without opening Config.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardModalBody: Same form as in Config Quick add. We prefilled another random site for this step.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardCreateIntroB: Creating here saves immediately and shows the tile on your current page.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardTileBody: Here is the new tour bookmark on your dashboard. It is removed when you finish the tour in Config.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardReturnBody: Click Next to return to Config → Bookmarks and remove all demo bookmarks.
config.configBookmarksTourSearchBody: Filter the bookmark list by name or URL. Clear the field to show everything again.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkBody: Select multiple bookmarks, then use Move to for page or category changes, plus pin, status, favicon refresh, or delete.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkDemoBody: We selected a few bookmarks so you can try Move to, pin, status, favicon refresh, or delete.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkEmptyBody: Select bookmarks with the checkboxes in the list to show bulk actions.
config.configBookmarksTourFaviconBody: Choose when bookmark icons refresh: on save or only manually.
config.configBookmarksTourSaveBody: Add & edit changes are not written until you click Save. Unsaved edits are highlighted.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupIntroBody: Remove temporary tour bookmarks from the editor and saved data.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupResumeBody: Welcome back — remove the temporary tour bookmarks from your library.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We remove the temporary tour bookmarks from the editor and from the saved page so your library stays unchanged.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupDoneBody: All tour bookmarks are removed. Your collection is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupKeptBody: Demo bookmarks may still be present. Delete them in the list or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.resetConfigFindersTourHint: Run the Finders tour again (once per install; completion is saved to your settings).
config.resetConfigFindersTourFailed: Could not start the Finders tour. Open the Finders tab first.
config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedTab: Could not start the Finders tour. Open the Finders tab first.
config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedDom: Could not start the Finders tour. The list is still loading — refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedReload: Could not start the Finders tour. Refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Finders tour. Use a wider window or turn off mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configFindersTourWelcomeBody: Finders are quick-search shortcuts to external sites — Google, DuckDuckGo, Wikipedia, and more. You trigger them from the dashboard with ? plus a shortcut key.
config.configFindersTourConceptBody: Each finder has a name, a search URL with %s as the placeholder for your query, and a one-letter shortcut. nextDash opens the finished URL in your browser — it does not search inside your bookmark list.
config.configFindersTourFieldsBody: Edit each row here: display name, full search URL (must include %s), lowercase shortcut (a–z), and optional comma-separated tags for filtering in config.
config.configFindersTourAddBody: Click + Add finder for a blank row. Change the URL and shortcut to match any search site you use regularly.
config.configFindersTourGoogleIntroBody: A common pattern is Google with URL https://www.google.com/search?q=%s. We prefer shortcut {preferred} if it is free; otherwise we suggest the next available letter. Next we can add this row — only if you agree.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentShortcutNo: Shortcut {preferred} is already used by another finder — we will use {shortcut} for this Google example instead.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentBody:
We can add a ready-made Google finder to your list now:

• Name: Google
• URL: https://www.google.com/search?q=%s
• Shortcut: {shortcut}

You still need to click Save in config to keep it. Nothing is sent to Google until you use the finder on the dashboard.
config.configFindersTourGoogleNoShortcut: All single-letter shortcuts are already used by finders. Free a letter or remove a finder, then try the tour again.
config.configFindersTourGoogleShortcutTaken: Shortcut {shortcut} was just taken by another finder. Pick a different shortcut manually.
config.configFindersTourGoogleAddedBody: Here is your Google finder. The URL uses %s where your search words go. On the dashboard, press ? then {shortcut} and your query — for example ?{shortcut} nextdash opens Google with that search.
config.configFindersTourGoogleSkippedBody: No problem — you can add finders yourself with + Add finder. Use %s in the URL where the search text should go, and pick a single-letter shortcut.
config.configFindersTourUsageBody: Press ? to open finder mode. Type {shortcut} and your words — e.g. ?{shortcut} nextdash — then Enter. The %s in the URL is replaced with your query. Enable “Include finders in search” under General → Advanced if you also want finders in normal search results.
config.configFindersTourMaintainBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Remove deletes after confirmation. Usage stats (uses · last used) help you see which finders you actually use.
config.configFindersTourSaveBody: Finder changes are stored when you click Save. If you added the Google example during this tour, save now to keep it after a refresh.

config.resetConfigStatsTourFailed: Could not start the Stats tour. Open the Stats tab first.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedTab: Could not start the Stats tour. Open the Stats tab first.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedDom: Could not start the Stats tour. Stats are still loading — refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedReload: Could not start the Stats tour. Refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Stats tour. Use a wider window or disable mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configStatsTourWelcomeBody: Below the intro line, this is your stats dashboard: quick links on the left and insight sections on the right. Everything here is read-only — after you save bookmarks or settings elsewhere, reopen this tab to refresh the numbers.
config.configStatsTourIndexBody: Use the quick links on the left to scroll to any block. On wide screens the index stays visible while you read the charts and tables on the right.
config.configStatsTourOverviewBody: Counts for pages, categories, bookmarks, URLs, and shortcuts — plus average opens per bookmark. Click ℹ for a short explanation of each metric.
config.configStatsTourScoreBody: A 0–100 health score with a colour bar. The list below explains penalties: never-opened bookmarks, stale items, duplicate URLs, shortcut conflicts, and more.
config.configStatsTourActivityBody: Lifetime opens for bookmarks active in the period, a count of active bookmarks, and a sparkline of when bookmarks were last opened (not individual opens). Switch week, month, 3 months, 6 months, or all time.
config.configStatsTourTopBody: Tables for most opened and most recently opened bookmarks, with page names and timestamps. Change the period filter to focus on recent usage or all-time leaders.
config.configStatsTourPagesBody: Compare bookmark counts and opens per page, then per category within pages. Use period buttons to limit stats to recent activity or view all time.
config.configStatsTourTagsBody: See tag coverage, unique tags, and which tags appear on the most bookmarks. Tables rank tags and the most opened tagged bookmarks.
config.configStatsTourShortcutsBody: See how many bookmarks have keyboard shortcuts and which shortcuts get the most opens — useful when tuning your search workflow.
config.configStatsTourRotBody: Find bookmarks you never opened, items stale in the chosen period, and recently added links. Tables list candidates to review or remove.
config.configStatsTourConflictsBody: Duplicate URLs and shortcut conflicts are counted here with detail rows. Open Health for deeper triage and one-click fixes on the dashboard.
config.configStatsTourSearchBody: Shows whether the search index is built and how status monitoring is configured. Reopen this tab after changing settings or bookmarks to see updated numbers.
config.configCategoriesTourWelcomeBody: Categories are the columns on your dashboard. Each page has its own list — pick a page, add or rename categories, drag to reorder, and remove ones you no longer need.
config.configCategoriesTourPageBody: Use the Page menu to edit categories for that dashboard page. Switch pages here without leaving the Categories tab.
config.configCategoriesTourAddBody: Click + Add category for a new row. Next we can add a temporary “news” category for practice — only if you agree.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoIntroBody: A short demo helps you see how categories appear on the dashboard. We can create “news” on this page now.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoConsentMessage: For this tour we add a temporary category named “news” on the current page. You will reorder it and remove it before the tour ends — nothing stays on your dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoAddedBody: Here is your “news” category. Change the name or emoticon anytime. Column order here matches the category tabs on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoSkippedBody: No demo category was added. Use + Add category when you are ready — you can still follow the rest of the tour.
config.configCategoriesTourFieldsBody: Edit the display name and optional two-character emoticon. The category id stays stable when you rename — bookmarks keep their link.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderIntroBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Next we move “news” to the first slot so you can see the tab shift on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderDoneBody: We moved “news” to the first position — check your dashboard: the category tab order follows this list. Drag the ⠿ handle anytime to change order yourself. Press and hold a category title (~500 ms) to rename it inline.
config.configCategoriesTourRemoveBody: Click Remove (red) on a row to delete that category. You confirm in a dialog; bookmarks can be moved, uncategorized, or deleted depending on your choice.
config.configCategoriesTourRemoveConfirmMessage: Remove the demo category “news” from this page? Bookmarks in it become uncategorized.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary “news” category now. Confirm in the next dialog — same flow as Remove on a normal row.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupConfirmMessag: We added “news” only for this tour. Remove it now so your categories stay unchanged.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo category “news” is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo category is still listed. Click Remove on the “news” row and confirm, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configCategoriesTourCleanupNoneBody: There is no demo category left on this page. Use Remove on any row when you want to delete a category — you confirm in a dialog first.
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourHint: Run the Categories tour again (once per install; completion is saved to your settings).
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourFailed: Could not start the Categories tour. Open the Categories tab first.
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourFailedTab: Could not start the Categories tour. Open the Categories tab first.
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourFailedDom: Could not start the Categories tour. Categories are still loading — refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourFailedReload: Could not start the Categories tour. Refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigCategoriesTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Categories tour. Use a wider window or disable mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configPagesTourWelcomeBody: Pages are separate bookmark workspaces on your dashboard. Each page has its own categories and bookmarks — add pages here, reorder them, and remove ones you no longer need.
config.configPagesTourListBody: Every row is one dashboard page. Drag the ⠿ handle to change tab order on the dashboard. The main page cannot be removed.
config.configPagesTourAddBody: Click + Add page for a new workspace. Next we can add a temporary demo page — only if you agree.
config.configPagesTourDemoIntroBody: A short demo shows how a new page appears on the dashboard. We can create one now.
config.configPagesTourDemoConsentMessage: For this tour we add a temporary page named “Tour demo”. You will see it on the dashboard and remove it before the tour ends — nothing stays behind.
config.configPagesTourDemoAddedBody: Here is your demo page in the list. Rename it anytime — the name is used on the dashboard too.
config.configPagesTourDemoSkippedBody: No demo page was added. Click + Add page when you are ready — you can still follow the rest of the tour.
config.configPagesTourNameBody: Edit the name in the row. It is shown on dashboard page tabs and in Page menus across Config.
config.configPagesTourDashboardIntroBody: New pages show up on the dashboard as tabs and in the Page menu when editing bookmarks. We switch to Bookmarks to point at the same list.
config.configPagesTourDashboardDoneBody: Your new page appears in this Page menu and as a tab on the dashboard (top bar). Switch with 1–9 or Shift+←/→. Click ← back to dashboard to see it live.
config.configPagesTourDashboardSkippedBody: Each page you add shows up here in Bookmarks and as a tab on the dashboard. Use the Page menu to edit bookmarks per page.
config.configPagesTourRemoveBody: Click Remove (red) on a row to delete that page and all its bookmarks. You confirm in a dialog first. The main page cannot be removed.
config.configPagesTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary demo page now. Confirm in the next dialog — same flow as Remove on a normal row.
config.configPagesTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We added a temporary page only for this tour. Remove it now so your dashboard stays unchanged.
config.configPagesTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo page is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configPagesTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo page is still listed. Click Remove on its row and confirm, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configPagesTourCleanupNoneBody: There is no demo page left. Use Remove on any row except the main page when you want to delete a page — you confirm in a dialog first.
config.resetConfigPagesTourHint: Show the Pages tour again the next time you open the Pages tab.
config.resetConfigPagesTourFailed: Could not start the Pages tour. Open the Pages tab first.
config.resetConfigPagesTourFailedTab: Could not start the Pages tour. Open the Pages tab first.
config.resetConfigPagesTourFailedDom: Could not start the Pages tour. Pages are still loading — refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigPagesTourFailedReload: Could not start the Pages tour. Refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigPagesTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Pages tour. Use a wider window or disable mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configCollectionsTourWelcomeBody: Dynamic collections are extra columns on your dashboard. Each collection shows bookmarks that match rules you define — by tag, category, or keyboard shortcut.
config.configCollectionsTourListBody: Saved collections appear here with their match logic (AND / OR) and rule count. Edit or delete any row — bookmarks themselves are never removed.
config.configCollectionsTourAddBody: Click + New collection to open the editor. Next we can pre-fill example rules for tag, category, and shortcut — only if you agree.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoIntroBody: The fastest way to learn is a short demo collection with one rule per field type.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoConsentMessage: We open the editor and add example rules for tag, category, and shortcut (OR logic). You save it for the tour and we remove it before the end — nothing stays on your dashboard.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoOpenedBody: The editor is open with three example rules. Each rule uses Tag, Category, or Shortcut — matching bookmarks appear in this collection on the dashboard.
config.configCollectionsTourDemoSkippedBody: Click + New collection to open the editor. Add rules with the field dropdown: Tag, Category, or Shortcut — then set includes/excludes and a value.
config.configCollectionsTourTagBody: Tag — match bookmarks that have a tag (comma-separated on each bookmark). Example: tag includes “tour-demo”. Values are lowercased when saved.
config.configCollectionsTourCategoryBody: Category — match bookmarks in a category column. Use the category id (same as in Config → Categories), not the display name.
config.configCollectionsTourShortcutBody: Shortcut — match bookmarks with a keyboard shortcut letter. Example: shortcut includes “a”. With OR logic, any matching rule is enough.
config.configCollectionsTourLogicBody: AND requires every rule to match; OR includes bookmarks that match any rule. The demo uses OR so tag, category, or shortcut matches are enough.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveIntroBody: Click Save to store the collection. It appears on the dashboard for the current page when bookmarks match.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveDoneBody: Your demo collection is saved. It appears in the list and on the dashboard as a dynamic column when rules match bookmarks.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveSkippedBody: Click Save in the editor when your rules are ready. Collections are stored in settings and show on the dashboard immediately.
config.configCollectionsTourSaveFailedBody: Fill in a name and at least one rule value, then click Save. Use OR logic so bookmarks matching any rule are included.
config.configCollectionsTourDashboardBody: Open the dashboard — matching collections show as extra columns next to your categories. Hover the column header to see which rules matched.
config.configCollectionsTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary demo collection now. Confirm in the next dialog — same as deleting any collection.

config.configCollectionsTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo collection is removed. Your dashboard is back to how it was before the tour.

config.resetConfigThemeTourFailedTab: Could not start the Theme tour. Open the Theme tab first.
config.resetConfigThemeTourFailedDom: Could not start the Theme tour. The editor is still loading — refresh the page and try again.
config.resetConfigThemeTourFailedReload: Could not start the Theme tour. Refresh the page and try again.

config.configThemeTourWelcomeBody: Fine-tune built-in palettes or create custom themes here. This tour adds a temporary demo theme, saves it, activates it on General, then removes it.
config.configThemeTourSubtabsBody: Switch between default dark/light palettes and your own custom themes. We work in Custom themes for this demo.
config.configThemeTourAddIntroBody: Click Add Custom Theme to start from the default starter colors. Next we create one for you automatically.
config.configThemeTourDemoIntroBody: We add a theme named “Tour demo” with a magenta accent so you can spot it in the list and preview.
config.configThemeTourDemoAddedBody: We created “Tour demo” with a distinct accent color. You can rename it in the list — it is saved to disk after the next step.
config.configThemeTourDemoFailedBody: Click Add Custom Theme to create a palette, then continue the tour.
config.configThemeTourPreviewIntroBody: The preview card shows how bookmarks and controls look with your palette. Adjust colors anytime before saving.
config.configThemeTourSaveIntroBody: Save colors writes custom themes to disk so they appear in General → Theme and on the dashboard.
config.configThemeTourSaveDoneBody: Your custom theme is saved. It now appears in General → Appearance. Next we switch there to activate it.
config.configThemeTourSaveFailBody: Click Save colors to write your custom theme to disk before continuing.
config.configThemeTourGeneralIntroBody: Switch to General → Appearance to choose which theme is active across the app.
config.configThemeTourGeneralHandoffBody: Saved themes are picked here under Theme. We pre-select the tour demo so you can see it live on Config and the dashboard.
config.configThemeTourSelectIntroBody: Custom themes appear in this list after you save them on the Theme tab. We apply the tour demo now.
config.configThemeTourSelectDoneBody: “Tour demo” is now your active theme. The dashboard uses it immediately — we remove it at the end of the tour.
config.configThemeTourSelectFailBody: Choose “Tour demo” in the Theme dropdown to apply your new palette.
config.configThemeTourCleanupIntroBody: Remove the temporary theme and restore your previous selection so nothing stays behind.
config.configThemeTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We remove the temporary “Tour demo” theme and restore your previous theme selection.
config.configThemeTourCleanupNoneBody: No demo theme remains. Custom themes you create here are always listed under General → Theme after saving.
config.configThemeTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo theme is removed and your previous theme is restored. Your own custom themes are unchanged.
config.configThemeTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo theme may still be present. Delete it on the Theme tab or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configThemeTourCleanupFailBody: Could not remove the demo theme automatically. Delete “Tour demo” in Custom themes on the Theme tab.
config.configTagsTourWelcomeBody: Tags group bookmarks across all pages. Manage them here — add them on each bookmark in the Bookmarks tab (comma-separated).
config.configTagsTourCloudBody: Popular tags appear larger in the cloud. Click a chip to jump to that tag in the list below.
config.configTagsTourListBody: Each row shows how many bookmarks use a tag. Rename merges tags globally; × removes a tag from every bookmark. Click the label to expand the bookmark list.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksIntroBody: Tags are set per bookmark in Config → Bookmarks. Next we can add a sample bookmark and tag it for you — only if you agree.
config.configTagsTourDemoConsentTitle: Try adding a tag on a new bookmark?
config.configTagsTourDemoConsentMessage: We can open the Bookmarks tab, add a temporary bookmark, and set the tag “tour-demo” in the Tags field — then show it here on the Tags tab. The bookmark is removed before the tour ends.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksAddedBody: A new bookmark is open on the right. Tags are comma-separated — we filled in “tour-demo”. Change the field anytime; tags are normalised to lowercase on save.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksFailedBody: Could not add the demo bookmark. Click + Add yourself, select the row, then type tags in the Tags field below.
config.configTagsTourBookmarksSkippedBody: Open + Add to create a bookmark, select it in the list, then type comma-separated tags in the Tags field on the right — for example work, dev, personal.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldIntroBody: The Tags field lives in the bookmark editor on the right. Comma-separated values become normalised tags when you save.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldBody: Select a bookmark in the list, then type comma-separated tags here — for example work, dev, personal. Tags are trimmed and lowercased when you save.
config.configTagsTourTagsFieldDoneBody: This Tags field is where you attach labels to a bookmark. We used “tour-demo” — add more with commas. They power search, filters, and dynamic collections.
config.configTagsTourResultIntroBody: Back on the Tags tab: every tag from your bookmarks appears in the cloud and list. We switch here to find your sample tag.
config.configTagsTourResultDoneBody: Here is “tour-demo” in your tag cloud and list. Click a tag to see which bookmarks use it, or rename and delete tags globally.
config.configTagsTourResultEmptyBody: After you save bookmarks with tags, they appear in the cloud and list here. Rename merges tags; delete removes them from every bookmark.
config.configTagsTourCleanupIntroBody: To leave your library unchanged, we remove the temporary bookmark from the Bookmarks tab now.
config.configTagsTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We added a temporary bookmark with tag “tour-demo” for this tour. Remove it now so your library stays unchanged.
config.configTagsTourCleanupDoneBody: The demo bookmark is removed. Your tag list is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configTagsTourCleanupKeptBody: The demo bookmark may still be on the current page in Bookmarks. Delete it there, or restart the tour from General → System tools.
config.configTagsTourCleanupNoneBody: No demo bookmark remains. Tags you add in Bookmarks show up here automatically after save.

config.helpIntro: This guide walks you through nextDash in plain language: how the dashboard feels day to day, where settings live, and which habits save time once you are past the first five minutes.
config.settingsSearchPromoBody: Find any setting, tab, or help section from here. Type a keyword and pick a result — or press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+K</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd+Shift+K</kbd> on Mac). <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> opens quick actions only.
config.helpPageWhatsNewIntro: A short recap of recent dashboard and config changes.
config.helpPageWhatsNewItems:
• Tidier long categories, aligned config & new-install defaults (v2026.07.18) — a category now shows only its first 15 bookmarks by default, with the rest behind a per-category + N more / show less toggle, so one big category no longer towers over the others; change the limit or turn it off under Config → General → Layout (smart collections are never capped, and expanding a category is remembered). The Configuration page now uses the same top bar and title size as the dashboard, inbox, and health views, so switching between them no longer makes the page jump, and its save row and tabs read as one seamless bar. New installs start on the near-black Midnight Ink theme (following your system light/dark) and no longer seed the Tech category or its Unraid/Phoronix bookmarks — existing dashboards keep their theme and bookmarks.
  • Dashboard ↔ config shortcut & compact General (v2026.07.17.2) — < (that's Shift+,) now jumps from the dashboard to config and back again, asking to confirm first if config has unsaved changes; it's listed on the cheat sheet (! / F1) and Config → Keyboard. A fresh first visit to Config → General also opens compact — Essentials with only Localisation expanded — until you set your own section layout.
  • Tours, spotlights, and promo balloons removed (v2026.07.17) — the onboarding wizard, the nine config-tab guided tours, the dashboard feature tour, and roughly twenty one-time discoverability balloons are gone; everything they taught is in the keyboard cheat sheet (! or F1) in more detail. First run now shows a short quick-start card instead (language, layout, weather, then a small checklist), and the rotating footer tips moved into a proper Tips & tricks section right here in Help, grouped by task and searchable like any other section. The settings search promo is the one balloon that stays. Getting started and several other Help sections were rewritten to match, and two missing translations (Help intro, custom themes info) were filled in.
  • Inbox snooze, keyboard triage & Health always-on (v2026.07.16) — Inbox can snooze links (3h / tomorrow / weekend / next week) with a Snoozed filter and z, gains Health-style keyboard navigation (j/k/g/G, Enter/p/r/n/z/d), per-row notes, mark-read plus bulk Mark all read / Clear read, and a preview loading pulse; promoting with status checks on immediately health-checks that URL. Health is always in the header (hide toggle removed), can optionally re-check in the background under Config → General → Status monitoring, opens Edit in the dashboard inline editor, and deep-link filters match the right rows again.

config.helpPageGettingStartedBody:
The first time you open nextDash, a quick-start card in the corner walks through three short steps: language and auto dark mode, how the grid is laid out, and whether to show the weather. Skip it whenever you like — nothing is locked in, and every setting it touches stays reachable under Config → General. After the steps it becomes a small checklist: add a bookmark, tag one, open config, and look at the keyboard shortcuts. Finish or dismiss it and it does not come back.

Once you're in, the essentials fit in half a minute:

  • > search — type part of a name, Enter opens the top result
  • + full new-bookmark form  ·  & one-line quick add on the dashboard (name | url | shortcut)
  • 0 Inbox  ·  * recent bookmarks  ·  ! or F1 keyboard cheat sheet
  • Ctrl+K quick actions  ·  Ctrl+Shift+K find any setting or help section

Most layout and behaviour lives under Config → General, and the ℹ button next to almost every setting explains what it does without leaving the form. After a new release you may see a one-time What's new summary; you can reopen it any time from Advanced → System → Onboarding & tips, which is also where you bring the quick-start card back.
config.helpPageConfiguringBody:
Settings are grouped into tabs — System (General, Theme, Backups, Stats, Keyboard), Dashboard (Pages, Categories, Bookmarks), Extras (Tags, Finders, Collections), and Help — with the active group highlighted and a dot on any group with unsaved changes (e.g. System ●). A breadcrumb under the tabs shows where you are (General › Layout), and the save row tells you whether the current tab needs an explicit Save or saves automatically (Collections and Finders save on their own). On a phone the tab bar collapses to a simpler set.

General is the control room for the whole dashboard, and its toolbar switches between three layers. Essentials covers Localization (language, date, time, weather), Appearance (theme, fonts, animations), Layout (Classic/Modern, density, columns, title), Bookmarks (display and behaviour), Smart Collections (which automatic groups are on), and Header & buttons (which footer and corner buttons show). Advanced adds finer tuning for the same areas plus a few that only live here: background images and fonts, Smart Collections limits, Diagnostics & status (health pings), Branding & identity (title, favicon), Search & input behaviour, and System & tools (reset buttons and What's new). All sections puts everything on one scrollable page for a full overview.

Like this Help tab and Stats, General has a sticky quick links sidebar next to the settings — opening a section from the sidebar or by clicking its title collapses whichever other section was open, so only one stays expanded at a time; on narrow screens the sidebar becomes a horizontal chip bar instead. Changes do not apply until you press Save, after which the dashboard refreshes in place without a full reload.
config.helpPageKeyboardBody:
Most dashboard keys can be rebound under Config → Keyboard: click a binding, press the new key combination, and conflicts with fixed shortcuts or other custom bindings are flagged before you save. A whole preset can be exported to a file and re-imported later, which is useful for keeping multiple installs in sync. The cheat sheet (! or F1) always reflects your current bindings and has its own search box for finding one quickly.

Grid navigation:

  • Tab, a click, G+digit, or the first arrow key starts navigation
  • ↑/↓/←/→ move the highlight  ·  Enter/Space opens
  • 1–9 jump to a page  ·  Shift+←/Shift+→ switch pages  ·  , page overview
  • . collapses or expands every category at once  ·  Esc clears the selection or cancels an unsaved drag

With a bookmark selected:

  • ; inline edit
  • Shift+M move  ·  Shift+T quick-tag  ·  Shift+D delete (with undo in the toast)
  • Home/End/Page Up/Page Down jump further through the grid

On a Mac, Cmd+C copies a selected bookmark's URL and Cmd+Home/End jump to the first or last page. Fixed shortcuts (like 0 for Inbox) are listed separately from your custom bindings so you always know what's safe to reassign.
config.helpPageSearchToolbarBody:
Search is really three modes behind one overlay, switchable by typing a prefix or clicking a tab at the top: > for normal search, : for commands, and ? for finders. A lone : opens grouped commands (bookmarks, navigation, layout, smart collections, settings) with recent commands floating to the top — try :layout modern, :density compact, :sort, :backup, :export, :inbox, or :quicktag to see how much of config has a matching command. Filters such as tag:work, category:news, status:online, and page:2 narrow normal-search results without touching the dashboard layout, and combine freely with plain text.

The dashboard footer holds a row of buttons for the actions you reach for most: + bookmark opens the full new-bookmark form, search opens the overlay in search mode, commands opens it in command mode, finders opens it in finder mode, recent lists your last-opened bookmarks, and the cheat sheet shows every shortcut with its own search box. Two more floating buttons appear in the corners when enabled: the tag cloud FAB (/) opens a popularity-scaled word cloud for multi-tag filtering, and the What's new star opens a short changelog the first time a release ships, or any time from here via Show what's new above. Which of these buttons are visible is configurable under General → Header & buttons — hide the ones you never use to keep the footer minimal.

Two different shortcuts are easy to confuse: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) runs quick actions only — save, jump to the dashboard — while Ctrl+Shift+K searches every setting and help section across all of config and expands the matching panel automatically.
config.helpPageOrganizingBody:
On the dashboard, bookmarks behave like a small spreadsheet: arrow keys move the selection, ; opens inline edit on the highlighted row, and a long press opens the same editor with touch. A plain click opens the bookmark itself, while dragging a row — from anywhere on it — reorders the bookmark within its category or drops it into another one; a drag never opens the editor, and a click never reorders. Grid navigation pauses while inline edit is open so you cannot accidentally jump away, and edits to smart-collection rows update the real bookmark everywhere it appears.

Pinned bookmarks always float to the top of their category and sort alphabetically among themselves; everyone else follows the category's sort mode — manual drag, A–Z, or Recent, switched via the chips in each category header. While a category is on A–Z or Recent its bookmarks can't be dragged to reorder — a hover tooltip, a not-allowed cursor, and a brief note explain to switch it back to manual order first. Bookmarks without a category land in an Other bucket at the end of the page. Long-press a category header to rename it, or drag the // prefix in its title to reorder categories; the same order can be edited in Config → Categories. Press . anywhere on the dashboard to collapse or expand every category at once. Command mode :sort applies to the focused category if you prefer the keyboard.

There are several ways to add a bookmark: + opens the full form, & adds one in a single line on the dashboard (name | url | shortcut), pasting a URL (Ctrl+V) offers a quick prompt, and the browser extension saves the current tab. The full form's Page and Category dropdowns each carry a + New… option, so you can create a page or category inline and save it straight away without first adding a bookmark. Every bookmark can carry a shortcut letter, tags, a note, a custom icon, and an optional status check that pings the URL to show online/offline state right on its row.
config.helpPageWorkspaceBody:
Config → Pages creates, renames, reorders (drag or the ↑/↓ buttons, auto-saved), and archives pages. Archiving hides a page from the header tabs without deleting its bookmarks, so nothing is lost if you bring it back later.

Config → Categories works the same way, plus merging: drag one category's bookmarks into another to combine them and remove the empty one. The order set here matches the dashboard exactly, and can also be changed by dragging the // prefix in a category's title on the dashboard.

Config → Bookmarks is built for bulk work: a filterable, sortable list on the left, a detail editor on the right, and a collapsible Context panel to switch page and category without losing your place in the list. Select multiple rows to move, pin, tag (add, replace, or remove), delete, or refresh favicons together, and conflict highlighting flags duplicate URLs or shortcuts before you save. Ctrl+Shift+K jumps to any setting from here, and Ctrl+K runs quick actions.
config.helpPageTagsCollectionsBody:
Tags are free-form labels added in config or inline on the dashboard, normalised on save (trimmed, lowercased, deduplicated) and suggested by autocomplete as you type an existing one. In search, tag:work filters results without rearranging the grid; on desktop, the tag cloud (/ or its corner button) colour-codes tags by how often they're used and lets you toggle several at once while the modal stays open, matching bookmarks with any selected tag (OR logic) — a clear button resets the filter in one click. Command mode :tag work lists matches in the palette only, without changing the dashboard.

Smart collections are automatic groups — Today, Recently opened, Stale bookmarks (not opened in a while), and Most used (ranked by open count) — each toggled per page with an optional item limit (0 = unlimited); a master switch under Essentials turns them all on or off at once, with per-page detail under Advanced. They sit alongside ordinary categories and collapse the same way. Turning on Tag collections under General → Smart Collections spawns one dynamic group per heavily-used tag, with a minimum bookmark count so rare tags do not clutter the dashboard.

Custom collections (Config → Collections) are rule-based instead: give one a name, an optional emoji, AND/OR match logic, and rules on tag, category, or shortcut. Each rule's value field autocompletes from the tags, categories, and shortcuts already in use, so you rarely have to type a full value. An AND collection with category:work and tag:urgent surfaces only bookmarks matching both; an OR collection with tag:reading and tag:later catches either. Matching bookmarks appear as read-only dashboard sections, sorted before ordinary categories, and save immediately with no separate Save button.
config.helpPageInboxBody:
Inbox is a lightweight capture list for links to read or sort later, separate from bookmark pages. Open it from the Inbox tab in the header, press 0 on the dashboard (search closed), or run :inbox.

Paste a URL on the dashboard (Ctrl+V) and choose Save to Inbox or Add bookmark — or set a default under General → Paste URL default (Ask every time, Always bookmark, or Always Inbox) to skip the prompt entirely. The browser extension can also save to Inbox, and duplicate URLs are rejected with a toast.

On the Inbox page, filter All/Unread, search, and browse by date group (Today, Yesterday, This week, Older). Each item can be opened, Promoted to a full bookmark (pre-fills the new-bookmark form with page and category to pick), or deleted with undo. New items stay unread until opened or triaged; a tab badge shows the unread count.

Triage walks items one by one, keyboard-only:

  • J/K move  ·  O/Enter open
  • P promote to a full bookmark  ·  R/Space keep (marks read)
  • D/Delete remove  ·  Esc close triage

Start it from the Triage button or :inbox triage. Toggle the tab itself under General → Enable Inbox page.
config.helpPageHealthStatusBody:
Status monitoring optionally pings bookmarks to show online/offline state right on their dashboard row. Enable it under General → Advanced → Status, choose whether to show ping detail and a loading spinner, and use Skip fast ping check if background noise is too high — useful on flaky networks or when you have many bookmarks.

For deeper triage, open the dashboard Health view (/#health). Summary cards total healthy, broken, duplicate, stale, and unchecked bookmarks; click one to filter the list, and search, status filters, sorting, and retest actions sit in one compact toolbar. Each row shows a 0–100 health score that factors in whether a bookmark has ever been opened, how stale it is, and whether its URL or shortcut conflicts with another bookmark, alongside repair actions: re-check status, detect redirect, refresh title, refresh favicon, or archive. Merging two duplicates keeps one row and folds the other's tags and notes into it.

Click any score badge — or press s — to see how it was reached: every bookmark starts at 100 and each issue shows what it costs. A repaired bookmark turns green straight away, and an applied redirect is checked against the new address before the row counts as healthy. Note that Retest statuses only checks bookmarks that have Check status switched on (off by default, set per bookmark in Config → Bookmarks) plus anything already flagged with an error; it says so when there is nothing to test.

The page is built for the keyboard: j/k or arrows move focus, Tab steps one row at a time, g/G jump to first/last, Enter opens the bookmark in config and o opens the URL. On the focused row, s shows the score breakdown, p re-checks, f refreshes the favicon, x selects and m opens more actions. The legend at the top of the page lists them all. The page follows your dashboard's layout and theme, so it feels like part of the same app rather than a separate tool.
config.helpPageAppearanceBody:
Pick a look under Essentials → Layout: Classic (dense, list-first), or Modern (card-based with more breathing room) — same underlying structure, different polish, and Modern is early-beta. Density has four levels — Compact, Comfortable, Dense, and Auto (adapts to screen and zoom) — and column count and dashboard title live in the same panel. Switch layout version from the dashboard with :layoutversion to try one before saving.

Advanced → Appearance adds background images or presets, a UI font (including an uploaded custom font file), and favicon harmonisation, which recolours mismatched site favicons so they don't clash with your theme. Auto dark mode follows the system theme. Theme colours live on their own Theme tab with live preview, packaged palettes, JSON import/export, and undo; a shortcut link elsewhere in config opens it directly.

The header's date/time/weather line is optional and configured under General: toggle date and time independently, with formats from compact numeric to long weekday names, and 24- or 12-hour clocks. With weather enabled, choose browser geolocation or a manual city, Celsius or Fahrenheit, and a refresh interval.

On narrow screens, portrait tablets, or touch devices, nextDash switches to a lighter chrome — the dashboard footer keeps just Search and + Bookmark, with commands and finders folded into the search overlay's >/:/? tabs. The cheat sheet and some footer buttons are desktop-only, and config on a phone focuses on the settings you're most likely to need on the go — the full split-view bookmark editor expects a wider window.
config.helpPageDataBackupsBody:
Server data lives in ./data by default — override with NEXTDASH_DATA_DIR for Docker volumes or multiple instances. Open dashboard tabs poll a revision endpoint so bookmark grids refresh when another tab saves changes, and link preview metadata is cached on the server and flushed periodically. When enabled, device-specific settings are stored in the browser's local storage, so one computer can keep different visual preferences than another.

Config → Backups handles the rest. A ZIP export includes pages, bookmarks, categories, finders, settings, and themes — import replaces everything, so export first (:backup opens the tab, :export downloads immediately). The write token and other environment variables are not part of the ZIP; they live in your server's environment, not in exported data.

Automatic backups keep a safety net on the server: once a week nextDash writes a full ZIP under data/auto-backups/ and keeps the latest 3, removing the oldest as new ones are made. The Automatic Backups section lists each one with its date and size, with Download, Restore (roll back to that backup in one click), and Delete buttons, a Back Up Now button, and a countdown to the next run. It's on by default and can be turned off with a single toggle. Keep data/ on a mounted volume so these survive container rebuilds.

You can also import a browser's HTML bookmark export (folders become categories, duplicates are skipped, with a preview before you commit) or export everything to CSV — name, URL, page, category, shortcut, tags, and notes — for spreadsheets or a quick audit outside nextDash.
config.helpPageFindersBody:
Finders are search shortcuts that send a query straight to an external site instead of your bookmarks — ?g nextdash searches Google for "nextdash", for example. Open finder mode with ?, or reach it through the finders footer button. Define finders under Config → Finders with a shortcut letter, a display name, and a URL containing %s where the query should be inserted; drag or use arrow keys to reorder, and duplicate shortcuts are flagged before you save.

Turn on Include finders in search and a bookmark sharing the same shortcut letter as a finder appears alongside it in normal search results too, so one keystroke can reach either. The Finders tab also tracks usage per finder, so you can see which ones you actually reach for.
config.helpPageSelfHostingBody:
The browser extension (in extension/) saves the current tab to nextDash. Install it unpacked in Chrome, set the server URL, and paste the write token if your server uses NEXTDASH_WRITE_TOKEN. The save form supports an optional shortcut (auto-suggested from the title), tags, and notes, warns about duplicate URLs, and can Save to Inbox instead of picking a page. If CORS is restricted, add your chrome-extension:// origin to NEXTDASH_CORS_ORIGINS.

nextDash has no built-in user accounts — anyone who can reach the URL can read and write data unless you protect it with a VPN, private network, or reverse-proxy authentication. Do not expose plain HTTP to the public internet. Set NEXTDASH_WRITE_TOKEN so write APIs require the X-NextDash-Token header (the dashboard and config pages inject it automatically once you're signed in via the browser), restrict NEXTDASH_CORS_ORIGINS for the extension, and tune activity logging with NEXTDASH_ACTIVITY_LOG (mutate, status, open, security, or off) — outbound fetches already validate public IPs to reduce SSRF risk. Docker Compose is the recommended way to run nextDash long-term; the production compose file mounts only ./data and serves CSS/JS from the image.

If bookmarks seem to vanish, check the page and category filters in config first — it's usually a filter, not data loss. Sorting surprises usually mean a category is in A–Z or Recent mode, or a pin is doing its job; search gaps often clear up with fuzzy mode or filters like tag:work. Extension save failures almost always trace back to the server URL, write token, or CORS; API 401 means a missing token, 429 means you hit a rate limit — outbound and API rate limits exist to protect the server, and settle down within a minute or two.

colors.palettesInfoMessage:
Three ways to edit colors on this tab:

• Dark and Light — change the fallback palettes for the classic dark/light themes in General → Appearance.

• Custom themes — create your own single-palette themes with Add Custom Theme. Each custom theme is one fixed look, not a day/night pair.

• Built-in named themes (Cherry Graphite, Nordic Frost, etc.) are picked in General → Appearance. Their packaged colors live in the server defaults unless you override palettes here.
colors.saveColorsInfoMessage:
Two separate save actions:

• Save colors (this tab) — writes palette edits from the Theme tab to the server. Use this after changing hex values or adding/removing custom themes.

• Save (config header) — stores General settings: which theme is active, layout, bookmarks, language, etc. It does not save color hex values from this tab.

Typical flow: edit colors → Save colors → pick the theme under General → Appearance → Save in the header.
colors.customThemesInfoMessage:
Custom themes are single palettes you create here.

• Add Custom Theme clones the default starter colors. Rename the theme and adjust colors in the editor on the right.

• To use it on the dashboard, select it under General → Appearance and click Save in the config header.

• Auto dark mode (General → Appearance) only works with built-in themes that have separate dark and light variants. It is disabled while a custom theme is selected — custom themes do not switch with your system appearance.

featureTour.step4Body: Press ">" or click the search button. Use filters like status:online, category:work or tag:dev. Your search history and saved searches are always available.
featureTour.step5Body: Set the number of columns that fits your screen. Favicons are the website icons next to each bookmark — handy for quick recognition.

featureTour.step7Body: Use arrow keys to navigate, Enter to open and ; to edit inline. Drag via the narrow handle strip on the left to reorder. In Config → Bookmarks you manage everything in bulk, import and export.
